product_name: Java SE (JDK) PQC Runtime (Oracle JDK 24 / Java 24)
product_brief: Oracle's Java 24 release with ML-KEM and ML-DSA implementations as steps toward post-quantum readiness for the Java platform.
pqc_support: Partial — press release only: announces quantum-resistant ML-KEM (JEP 496) and ML-DSA (JEP 497) implementations as an "important step towards post-quantum readiness" and "eventual delivery of PQC support"
pqc_capability_description: Per Oracle press release, Java 24 provides JEP 496 (ML-KEM, quantum-resistant Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism) and JEP 497 (ML-DSA, standardized by NIST in FIPS 204). Described as steps toward post-quantum readiness and eventual full PQC support for the Java platform. JEP 478 KDF API (Preview) also supports quantum-computing preparation.
primary_platforms: Java SE / JDK; Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
pqc_roadmap_details: JEP 496 and JEP 497 are described as an important step towards post-quantum readiness and the eventual delivery of PQC support for the Java platform; no timeline given.

evidence.PQC Support: This feature is an important step towards post-quantum readiness and the eventual delivery of post-quantum crypto (PQC) support for the Java platform
evidence.PQC Capability Description: providing an implementation of the quantum-resistant Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA)
evidence.Latest Version: Oracle today announced the availability of Java 24 , the latest version of the world's number one programming language
evidence.Crypto Primitives: providing an implementation of the quantum-resistant Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM)
evidence.Signature Schemes: it has been standardized by the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in FIPS 204
evidence.PQC Roadmap Details: an important step towards post-quantum readiness and the eventual delivery of PQC support for the Java platform
